The rapid adoption of digital assets by institutional investors has created an urgent need for an audit framework that can provide reliable assurance in a complex transaction environment. Although hash functions are well established, they have not been widely used in the construction of coherent, auditable evidence chains for dynamic event-driven systems. A Chain-Hash Audit Framework (CHAF) is proposed. In contrast to normal hash-chain logging, which directly links raw log entries, CHAF inserts the authorization status, the time stamp, and the life cycle property prior to the recursive hash binding. In order to avoid relying solely on hash recursion, the framework adds signed checkpoints, write-once storage, and external timestamp anchoring, thus creating a tamper-evident and externally verifiable evidence chain. This architecture allows auditors to traverse the business history of a digital asset system in a continuous structure and semantics. The formal design of CHAF is given in this paper, including data structure, authentication protocol, embedded reconstruction mechanism, and role based access control. Through a prototype implementation configured around a digital asset management workload, the framework reduces audit trail reconstruction time by more than 70% compared to traditional log-based approaches, and provides cryptographic verification of tamper evidence.

Higher education web systems manage highly sensitive student and academic data that are protected under the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA). However, many institutions continue to rely on perimeter-based security models, coarse-grained access control, and mutable audit logging mechanisms that are increasingly inadequate in distributed, cloud-enabled, and API-driven environments. These limitations expose academic systems to unauthorized access, compliance risks, and insufficient accountability. This paper proposes a comprehensive Zero Trust security framework that integrates FERPA-aligned data governance with identity-centric access control, secure application programming interfaces, and tamper-evident audit logging for higher education web systems. The proposed approach eliminates implicit trust assumptions by enforcing continuous authentication and authorization based on identity attributes, contextual information, and policy-driven governance rules. Secure APIs act as controlled access points to institutional data, while cryptographically chained, append-only audit logs ensure integrity, non-repudiation, and regulatory audit readiness. The framework is evaluated using simulated higher education access scenarios, comparing traditional perimeter-based systems with the proposed Zero Trust architecture. Results demonstrate significant improvements in access control precision, unauthorized access reduction, FERPA compliance coverage, and audit log integrity. The findings highlight the effectiveness of embedding regulatory compliance directly into system architecture rather than treating it as an external administrative requirement. This study contributes a unified, scalable, and reproducible model for securing academic web systems and advancing compliant data governance through Zero Trust principles.

"},{"DOI":"10.2139/ssrn.7307198","title":["Residual-Shadow Telemetry for Tamper-Evident Industrial Monitoring"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2026]]},"type":"posted-content","abstract":"Security controls can establish that telemetry arrived, that a message originated from a holder of a key, or that a stored record was not altered after collection. Those properties do not establish that a value remained unchanged while traversing a compromised telemetry path. This paper studies Residual-Shadow Telemetry (RST), a dualroute architecture in which a live observation and an intentionally delayed copy are reconciled by an independent witness. The design uses four verdicts-MATCH, MISMATCH, ABSENT, and UNRESOLVED-and prohibits positive assurance when an event cannot be evaluated. The study asks three questions: where an optional statistical plausibility layer is applicable on industrial control system data; how route dependence changes the claimed dual-route availability benefit; and where the architecture fails under common-cause or source compromise. A pilot analysis of a 19,999-sample clean window from each of 51 Secure Water Treatment (SWaT) tags found that 3 tags (5.9%) met the stated statistical screening conditions; 27 were excluded for plateau behavior and 21 for binary or effectively discrete behavior. Analytic correction of the route model shows that, for marginal loss p = 0.5%, joint loss equals p^2 only when route-failure correlation rho is zero; at rho = 0.6, joint loss is 0.301%, not 0.351%. Simulation results further show that when both routes carry the same forged stream, differential checks lose discriminating input and RST can grant false route-consistency assurance. RST is therefore best understood as a bounded path-integrity mechanism, not a truth oracle or a complete attack detector."},{"DOI":"10.37665/ppdgzde20978","title":["Tamper Proof, Tamper Evident Encryption Technology"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2013,1]]},"container-title":["Pan Pacific Symposium"],"type":"journal-article","abstract":"ABSTRACT Hardly a week goes by where there isn’t a report of cyber-crime having occurred. While the internet is convenient for many regular on-line activities, for example: Information searches, goods purchasing, sales, airline and hotel reservations, banking, bill-pay, driving directions and telephone/address look-up. It is the ease at which this information is so readily available that makes it vulnerable to attack. One solution would be to completely isolate the computer applications. However, most applications cannot perform their function in isolation. In order to prevent cyber crimes from occurring on server level products, IBM and Gore 1 have collaborated on a state-of-the-art physical security package to protect the hardware components of a cryptographic coprocessor module. 2 3 This package meets the highest level of physical security requirements contained in the U.S. Government Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 140-2 Security Requirements for Cryptographic Modules- (Level 4), and supports the overall attainment of FIPS 140-2 (Level 4) for the cryptographic coprocessor. This is the highest level of encryption technology which is allowed outside of the government or military. The packaging technology includes tamper response where any attempt at physically gaining access would render the cryptographic module useless. This paper will provide an overview of the protection features of the assembly and the manufacturing processes used to manufacture the product."},{"DOI":"10.1109/etfi68128.2026.11484826","title":["SecureChainFS: A Blockchain-Augmented File Transfer System with Tamper-Evident Audit Trails"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2026,2,12]]},"container-title":["2026 International Conference on Emerging Technologies and Future Innovations (ETFI)"],"type":"proceedings-article"},{"DOI":"10.35542/osf.io/d2jtc_v1","title":["Conformance Architecture for Network-Isolated Examinations on Candidate Devices with Tamper-Evident Transcripts"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2026,5,8]]},"type":"posted-content","abstract":"

Restricted-but-online examinations on candidate devices depend on endpoint restrictions that cannot reliably prevent network-mediated assistance or access to unauthorized device-local resources. This paradigm creates integrity risks from both exposure channels, and reliability risks from differential disruption that introduces construct-irrelevant variance. This paper specifies an execution protocol and reference architecture, presented as an implementation-neutral conformance profile, that defines Verified Network Isolation and Verified Local Restriction as mandatory start conditions for examinations on candidate devices while preserving courseware workflows. Under the protocol, examinations are packaged as Sealed Examination Packages and unlocked only upon proctor authorization and verification; the Exam Runner executes locally, produces a tamper-evident Execution Transcript, and defers connectivity restoration for upload, receipt issuance, and reconciliation under a Conformance Manifest. The contributions include a state-modeled execution protocol with named artifacts and defined state transitions, a supervised adversary model with a tier-bounded analytical security argument, a comparative evaluation framework with minimum reporting fields, and a minimum viable prototype scope with feasibility checks. Claims are conditional on the declared isolation tier and should be interpreted as analytical reductions in risk surfaces rather than absolute security assurances.

"},{"DOI":"10.2139/ssrn.7261059","title":["SpecAgent: An LLM-Driven Large-Scale Spectrum-Access Agent with Tamper-Evident Decisions"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2026]]},"type":"posted-content","abstract":"The radio spectrum is a scarce and heavily contested resource, and traditional dynamic spectrum access and radio resource management struggle to generalize across heterogeneous bands, large-scale topologies, and changing regulations. This paper presents SpecAgent, an LLM-driven large-scale spectrum-access agent that unifies a curricular contrastive spectrum-state encoder (CCSE), an RSS-text aligner, and a reasoningaction loop with tool use. CCSE learns label-efficient representations of radio spectrum state, the aligner projects occupancy maps and natural-language policies into a shared semantic space, and the loop emits interpretable access decisions augmented with tamperevident watermarks for accountability. Experiments on a metropolitan RSS dataset and a 10k-cell simulator show that SpecAgent attains an occupancy-prediction MAE of 0.058 and F1 of 0.88, a normalized spectral efficiency of 0.89, an SLA violation rate of 0.03, and a per-cell latency of 6.3 ms, slightly outperforming strong LLM-based baselines while remaining robust to policy changes."},{"DOI":"10.1109/sp.2010.19","title":["Tamper Evident Microprocessors"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2010]]},"container-title":["2010 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy"],"type":"proceedings-article"},{"DOI":"10.35542/osf.io/d2jtc_v2","title":["Conformance Architecture for Network-Isolated Examinations on Candidate Devices with Tamper-Evident Transcripts"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2026,5,12]]},"type":"posted-content","abstract":"

"},{"DOI":"10.18280/jesa.590215","title":["TALL-Detect: A Transformer and LLM-Augmented Framework for Tamper-Evident and Explainable Secure Log Analysis"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2026,2,28]]},"container-title":["Journal Européen des Systèmes Automatisés"],"type":"journal-article"},{"DOI":"10.66053/voice.v4i1.479","title":["A Tamper-Evident Audit Logging Framework for Decentralized Single Sign-On: Prototype Design and Evaluation in Education-Oriented Digital Services"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2026,4,18]]},"container-title":["Journal of Vocational, Informatics and Computer Education"],"type":"journal-article","abstract":"Purpose – This study aims to design, implement, and evaluate a prototype framework for tamper-evident audit logging in a decentralized single sign-on environment for education-oriented digital services. It addresses the risk that detailed authentication and session records remain stored in mutable off-chain systems, while storing complete audit data on-chain may increase costs and privacy exposure. Methods – The study adopted an artifact-based prototype design and evaluation approach. The prototype combined PostgreSQL-based off-chain audit storage, deterministic snapshot construction, canonical JSON serialization, SHA-256 hashing, Merkle root generation, and blockchain anchoring through the AuditAnchor smart contract on the Polygon Amoy testnet. The evaluation was conducted in a controlled prototype environment through tamper-detection testing, latency benchmarking, snapshot and proof performance measurements, storage-growth observations, and anchoring cost analysis. Findings – Post-anchoring record modification, deletion, and insertion consistently produce root mismatches. Across the evaluated workloads, snapshot construction remained below 0.4 s for up to 5,000 records, proof verification remained lightweight, and anchoring consumed 49,953 gas per transaction under the tested setup. Research implications – The prototype suggests that education-oriented multi-service environments may benefit from keeping detailed audit data off-chain while anchoring compact integrity commitments on-chain to support audit reviews, cross-service access tracing, and post-incident verifications. Originality – This study contributes a prototype-level integration of decentralized SSO, deterministic off-chain audit snapshots, and on-chain Merkle-root anchoring for audit verification"},{"DOI":"10.1533/9780857095664.2.220","title":["Tamper-evident food and beverage packaging"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2012]]},"container-title":["Emerging Food Packaging Technologies"],"type":"book-chapter"},{"DOI":"10.70917/ijcisim-2026-4475","title":["Trust-Guided Weighted Federated Averaging with Tamper-Evident Audit Logging for Robust Intrusion Detection on CICIoT2023"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2026,8,8]]},"container-title":["International Journal of Computer Information Systems and Industrial Management Applications"],"type":"journal-article","abstract":"Federated learning is a promising approach for Internet of Things intrusion detection because it enables collaborative model training without centralizing sensitive traffic data. However, federated intrusion detection remains vulnerable to non-IID client distributions, poisoned updates, and unreliable clients that can degrade the global detector. This paper presents a three-part framework for robust intrusion detection on CICIoT2023: a trust-guided weighted federated averaging scheme, a tamper-evident audit logging layer, and a poisoning-aware evaluation protocol. The proposed Trust-Guided Weighted Federated Averaging with Audit Logging (TGWFA-AL) combines validation-based trust, directional agreement of updates, and temporal trust adaptation using an exponential moving average to reduce the influence of suspicious clients over time. A tamper-evident audit trail records per-round model provenance using cryptographic hashes, trust components, filtering decisions, and aggregation weights, while storing raw models off-chain when needed to control cloud cost. The manuscript defines the threat model precisely, includes robust aggregation baselines beyond FedAvg, and supports both binary and multi-class evaluation with macro-averaged metrics. The numerical results, ablations, and overhead values in this draft are synthetic example values intended to make the manuscript structurally complete; they must be replaced with empirical outputs from the human author’s experiments before submission. "},{"DOI":"10.1109/sist61674.2026.11596448","title":["SME-ERP-X: An Integrated AI/ML-Tamper-Evident Audit Ledger-Digital Twin ERP Architecture with Financial Feasibility Analysis for SMEs"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2026,5,13]]},"container-title":["2026 IEEE 6th International Conference on Smart Information Systems and Technologies (SIST)"],"type":"proceedings-article"},{"DOI":"10.1145/2591635.2667184","title":["AEGIS"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2014]]},"container-title":["25th Anniversary International Conference on Supercomputing Anniversary Volume -"],"type":"proceedings-article"},{"DOI":"10.5220/0002997301960205","title":["HTEE: AN HMAC BASED TAMPER EVIDENT ENCRYPTION"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2010]]},"container-title":["Proceedings of the International Conference on Security and Cryptography"],"type":"proceedings-article"},{"DOI":"10.1007/978-3-030-77764-7","title":["Evolution of Smart Sensing Ecosystems with Tamper Evident Security"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2021]]},"type":"book"}],"items-per-page":25,"query":{"start-index":0,"search-terms":null}}}
